ideas.name: Bitcoin high-funding fade
ideas.claim: Short Bitcoin when the last settled eight-hour funding rate exceeds 0.05%, and exit after seven days.
ideas.quote: BTC: short when funding > 0.05%, hold 7 days — +6.89%

rules.entry: Short when the last settled eight-hour funding rate is above 0.05%.

ideas.claimed_result: The BTCUSDT perpetual futures backtest reports +6.89% return, 63.97% maximum drawdown and 42 trades from 2020-01-01 to 2026-10-01. It includes fees, slippage and funding payments; these are not CFD results.

ideas.name: Bitcoin negative-funding long
ideas.claim: Buy Bitcoin when the last settled eight-hour funding rate is negative, and exit after seven days.
ideas.quote: BTC: long when funding < 0, hold 7 days — +333.12%

rules.entry: Go long when the last settled eight-hour funding rate is below zero.

ideas.claimed_result: The BTCUSDT perpetual futures backtest reports +333.12% return, 40.84% maximum drawdown and 155 trades from 2020-01-01 to 2026-10-01. It includes fees, slippage and funding payments; these are not CFD results.

ideas.name: Bitcoin top-decile funding weakness
ideas.claim: Bitcoin funding in the top decile of its own historical distribution was followed by a negative median 72-hour return.
ideas.quote: On BTC, top-decile funding was followed by a negative median return at 72 hours and a hit rate well below chance.

rules.entry: Funding reaches or exceeds the 90th percentile of its own history; a trade entry is not stated.
rules.exit: Price effect measured after 72 hours; a trade exit is not stated.
rules.filters: Funding percentile calculated using data available at the observation time.

ideas.claimed_result: Across 37 non-overlapping episodes from 2024-05-15 to 2026-07-13, the median 72-hour Bitcoin return was −1.18%; 40.5% of episodes ended higher.
